address.en: to deal with or try to solve a problem

amount.en: how much there is of something

antecedent.en: something that existed or happened before and led to something else

anticipated.en: expected or predicted that something would happen

approaching.en: coming nearer in time or space

authorize.en: to give official permission for something

blemish.en: a small mark or flaw that spoils how something looks

brittle.en: hard but easily broken or cracked

common.en: happening often or found in many places

complicate.en: to make something more difficult to understand or deal with

constant.en: happening all the time or staying the same

decorative.en: made to look attractive; used as decoration

defect.en: a fault or flaw in something

defend.en: to protect, or to argue in support of something

delicate.en: easily damaged or broken; fine and fragile

describe.en: to say what something is like

diagram.en: a simple drawing that shows how something works or is arranged

dismissed.en: decided something was not important or worth considering

distant.en: far away in space or time

distorted.en: changed something so it is no longer true or accurate

dormant.en: not active now but able to become active later

drawings.en: pictures made with a pencil or pen

endorse.en: to publicly approve of or support something

estimate.en: to guess an amount or value based on information

evidence.en: facts or signs that show something is true

exploited.en: used something fully to gain an advantage

familiar.en: well known to you; seen or heard before

forthcoming.en: about to happen or appear soon

harnessed.en: controlled and used something, such as a natural force, for a purpose

historic.zh: 歷史性的；有歷史意義的

ignore.en: to pay no attention to something

illustration.en: a picture or example that explains something

innocent.en: not guilty; not meant to cause harm

irrelevant.en: not connected to or important for the subject

justify.en: to show that something is right or reasonable

mark.en: a spot, sign, or trace left on something

mitigate.en: to make something bad less severe

obsolete.en: no longer used because something newer exists

outline.en: a line showing the shape of something, or a short summary of main points

permanent.en: lasting forever or for a very long time

predict.en: to say what will happen in the future

quantity.en: an amount or number of something

rejected.en: refused to accept or believe something

remedy.en: to correct or fix a problem

remnant.en: a small part that remains of something

sanction.en: to give official approval or permission for something

signs.en: things that show something exists or is happening

simplified.en: made something easier to understand or do

summaries.en: short statements of the main points

utilized.en: used something for a practical purpose

validate.en: to prove that something is true or correct

valuable.en: worth a lot of money or very useful

withheld.en: kept something back; refused to give
